text: The first ionization enthalpy of Na, Mg and Si, respectively, are : 496, 737 and $786\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The first ionization enthalpy ($\mathrm{kJ}\quad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$) of $\mathrm{Al}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Al ($[\mathrm{Ne}]3s^{2}3p^{1}$) loses a 3p electron, which is higher in energy and shielded by the filled 3s subshell, whereas Mg ($[\mathrm{Ne}]3s^{2}$) loses a more penetrating electron from a fully filled 3s subshell. So the first ionization enthalpy of Al is less than that of Mg, $737\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Al has a higher nuclear charge than Na in the same period, so its first ionization enthalpy is greater than that of Na, $496\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$496<\Delta _{i}H(\mathrm{Al})<737\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Among the options only $577\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ lies in this range; 768 and 856 exceed the value for Mg and 487 is below that for Na.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: The reaction of zinc with excess of aqueous alkali, evolves hydrogen gas and gives :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Zinc dissolves in excess of aqueous alkali.

$\mathrm{Zn}+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}⟶[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}]^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_{2}↑$ (Tetrahydroxozincate(II) ion)

However, this reaction in NCERT is given as

$\mathrm{Zn}+2\mathrm{NaOH}⟶\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{ZnO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2}↑$

$\mathrm{ZnO}_{2}^{2-}$ is anhydrous form of $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}]^{2-}$.

$\mathrm{ZnO}_{2}^{2-}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}⇌[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}]^{2-}$

So in aqueous medium best answer of this question is $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}]^{2-}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text: In following pairs, the one in which both transition metal ions are colourless is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Sc}^{+3}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}$ are colourless as they contain no unpaired electron. Whereas the transition metal ions $\mathrm{Cu}^{+2},\mathrm{Ti}^{+3},\mathrm{V}^{+2}$ and $\mathrm{Mn}^{+2}$ are coloured as they contain unpaired electrons. 

The unpaired electron from lower energy $d$ orbital gets excited to a higher energy $d$ orbital on absorbing light of frequency which lies in visible region. The colour complementary to light absorbed is observed.

text: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ being a powerful oxidant can oxidize, thiosulphate almost quantitatively, to sulphate. In this reaction overall change in oxidation state of manganese will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In neutral or Faintly alkaline medium, thiosulphate is oxidised almost quantitatively to sulphate ion according to reaction given below, 

$8\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+3\mathrm{S}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to 8\mathrm{MnO}_{2}+6\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}$

 Here the $\mathrm{Mn}$ changes from $\mathrm{Mn}^{+7}$ to $\mathrm{Mn}^{+4}$

Thus overall change in its oxidation number would be of 3 .

text: Which among the following pairs of the structures will give different products on ozonolysis? (Consider the double bonds in the structures are rigid and not delocalized.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the ring double bonds fixed, each structure behaves as a cyclic triene. Ozonolysis cleaves every C=C, and each ring C–C single bond survives inside a 1,2-dicarbonyl fragment: a ring carbon carrying H becomes $-\mathrm{CHO}$ and one carrying $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ becomes $-\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$.

o-Xylene (option C): in the structure where the two methyl-bearing carbons are joined by a single bond, the fragments are $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCOCH}{}_{3}$ and 2 $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$; in the structure where they are joined by a double bond, the fragments are 2 $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCHO}$ and $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$. The two structures give different products.

m-Xylene (option A): the methyl-bearing carbons are never adjacent, so each pairs with an H-bearing carbon in both structures, giving 2 $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCHO}$ and $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$ each time.

p-Xylene (option B): both structures give 2 $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCHO}$ and $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$.

Toluene (option D): both structures give $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCHO}$ and 2 $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text:
Resistance of a conductivity cell (cell constant $129\mathrm{m}^{-1}$) filled with $74.5\mathrm{ppm}$ solution of $\mathrm{KCl}$ is $100\Omega$ (labelled as solution 1). When the same cell is filled with $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution of $149\mathrm{ppm}$, the resistance is $50\quad \Omega$ (labelled as solution 2). The ratio of molar conductivity of solution 1 and solution 2 is i.e. $\frac{\wedge _{1}}{\wedge _{2}}=x\times 10^{-3}$. The value of $x$ is $__________. ($Nearest integer)

Given, molar mass of $\mathrm{KCl}$ is $74.5\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{l}{A}=129\mathrm{m}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{KCl}$ solution $1\Rightarrow 74.5\mathrm{ppm},\mathrm{R}_{1}=100\Omega$

$\mathrm{KCl}$ solution $2\Rightarrow 149\mathrm{ppm},\mathrm{R}_{2}=50\Omega$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Here,}\dfrac{ppm_{1}}{ppm_{2}}=\dfrac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}=\left (\dfrac{w_{1/M_{0}}}{V}\times \dfrac{V}{w_{2/M_{0}}}\right ) \\ \dfrac{\Lambda _{1}}{\Lambda _{2}}=\dfrac{k_{1}\times \frac{1000}{M_{1}}}{k_{2}\times \frac{1000}{M_{2}}} \\ =\dfrac{k_{1}}{k_{2}}\times \dfrac{M_{2}}{M_{1}} \\ =\dfrac{50}{100}\times 2 \\ =\dfrac{\Lambda _{1}}{\Lambda _{2}}=1000\times 10^{-3} \\ =1000 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text:
The minimum uncertainty in the speed of an electron in an one dimensional region of length $2\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{o}}$ (Where $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{o}}=$ Bohr radius $52.9\mathrm{pm}$) is $_________$ $\mathrm{km}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

(Given : Mass of electron = 9.1 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$, Planck's constant h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Heisenberg's uncertainty principle

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{x}\times \Delta \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{x}}\geq \dfrac{h}{4π} \\ \Rightarrow 2\mathrm{a}_{0}\times \mathrm{m}\Delta \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}=\dfrac{h}{4π}\text{(minimum)} \\ \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}=\dfrac{h}{4π}\times \dfrac{1}{2a_{0}}\times \dfrac{1}{m} \\ =\quad 6.63\times 10^{-34} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} 4\times 3.14\times 2\times 52.9\times 10^{-12}\times 9.1\times 10^{-31} \\ =548273\mathrm{ms}^{-1} \\ =548.273\mathrm{kms}^{-1} \\ =548\mathrm{kms}^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

text:
When 600 mL of 0.2 M HNO$_{3}$ is mixed with $400\mathrm{mL}$ of 0.1 M NaOH solution in a flask, the rise in temperature of the flask is $___________$ $\times 10^{-2}{}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$.

(Enthalpy of neutralisation $=57\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and Specific heat of water $=4.2\mathrm{JK}^{-1}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$) (Neglect heat capacity of flask)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
HNO$_{3}$

600 mL × 0.2 M = 120 m mol 

 NaOH

 400 mL × 0.1 M = 40 m mol 


[IMG]


Heat liberated from reaction

$=40\times 10^{-3}\times 57\times 10^{3}\mathrm{J}\ldots (1)$

Heat gained by solution $=mC\Delta T$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{m}=\text{mass of solution}=\mathrm{V}\times \mathrm{d} & =1000\times 1 \\  \\ =1000\mathrm{g} \end{array}$

Heat gained by solution $=1000\times 4.2\times \Delta \mathrm{T}\ldots (2)$

From (1) and (2)

Heat liberated $=$ Heat gained

$40\times 10^{-3}\times 57\times 10^{3}=1000\times 4.2\times \Delta T$

$\Delta T=54\times 10^{-2}{}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

(Rounded off to the nearest integer)

text:
If $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ gas is bubbled through water at $303\mathrm{K}$, the number of millimoles of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ gas that dissolve in 1 litre of water is $__________. ($Nearest Integer)

(Given : Henry's Law constant for $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ at $303\mathrm{K}$ is $46.82\mathrm{k}$ bar and partial pressure of $\mathrm{O}_{2}=0.920$ bar)

(Assume solubility of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ in water is too small, nearly negligible)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}\times \mathrm{X}$

$0.920\mathrm{bar}=46.82\times 10^{3}\mathrm{bar}\times \frac{\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{of}\mathrm{O}_{2}}{\mathrm{mol}\text{of}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}$

$0.920=46.82\times 10^{3}\times \frac{\text{mol of O}_{2}}{1000/18}$

$0.920=46.82\times 18\times n_{O_{2}}$

$\frac{0.920}{46.82\times 18}=n_{O_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow n_{O_{2}}=1.09\times 10^{-3}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{of}\mathrm{O}_{2}=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift

$=282\times 10^{-16}$

$\therefore$ Ans. 282

In bromination of Propyne, with Bromine, 1, 1, 2, 2-tetrabromopropane is obtained in 27% yield. The amount of 1, 1, 2, 2-tetrabromopropane obtained from 1 g of Bromine in this reaction is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-1} g. ($Nearest integer)

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


2 moles $\mathrm{Br}_{2}\equiv 1$ mole 1,1,2,2-tetrabromopropane $\frac{1}{160}$ mole $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$

$\equiv \frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{160}$ mole 1,1,2,2-tetrabromopropane

But yield of reaction is only $27%$

text: $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$ should be an inner orbital complex. Ignoring the pairing energy, the value of crystal field stabilization energy for this complex is $(-)$ $____________$ $\Delta _{0}$. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\left [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})^{6}\right ]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is present in (+3) oxidation state $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{III})\Rightarrow$ inner orbital complex $\Rightarrow d^{5}$ (with pairing)

Configuration $\Rightarrow t_{2g}^{5}$

CFSE $=5\times \frac{-2}{5}\Delta _{0}=-2\Delta _{0}$
